## Your own placement {#find-your-own-percentile .smaller .output-8}

<!-- The placement slide of both slide decks, with a cell that reruns
     try_spec(). The first line differs by format: the full-day slides place the
     specification that was submitted, the part-day slides the one that the
     participant would defend. Keyed on the `deck:` map in the YAML of each slide deck;
     the cell sits outside every conditional span. -->

::: {.small}
- Rerun `try_spec()` with [the choices that you submitted]{.content-visible when-meta="deck.day"}[the specification that you would defend]{.content-visible unless-meta="deck.day"}, in the cell below[ or in your IDE workspace]{.content-visible unless-meta="deck.short"}: its last line places your estimate on the curve
- The placement counts the specifications of the curve whose estimate lies further below zero than yours. For the reference specification it is `r sum(curve$b_pp < curve_ref$b_pp - 1e-9)`: nothing on the curve lies further below zero, and the logit without covariates ties with it
- The same count places the published result and the five analysts
:::

```{webr}
#| autorun: false
# Type the arguments of your specification; run as it stands, this is the
# reference specification
try_spec()
```

::: notes
Now you are placed yourself. Type the arguments of [the choices that you submitted]{.content-visible when-meta="deck.day"}[the specification that you would defend, perhaps the one that you tried last,]{.content-visible unless-meta="deck.day"} into the cell and run it. The last line of the output is your placement, the number of the sixty-four specifications of the curve whose gap lies further below zero than yours. For the reference specification it is zero, because nothing on the curve lies further below zero, and the logit without covariates ties with it. Each of you can now say where your estimate stands among sixty-four justifiable alternatives, and a sentence of that kind, saying where the estimate sits among the specifications of a curve and how the curve was built, is a way of reporting a robustness check that a journal would accept.
:::
